title: Chromatin accessibility during human first-trimester neurodevelopment.
authors: Mannens, Camiel C A; Hu, Lijuan; Lonnerberg, Peter; Schipper, Marijn; Reagor, Caleb C; Li, Xiaofei; He, Xiaoling; Barker, Roger A; Sundstrom, Erik; Posthuma, Danielle; Linnarsson, Sten
one_liner_zh: 该文利用多组学与卷积神经网络预测人脑发育中增强子内的转录因子结合位点，虽聚焦染色质可及性而非直接TF-DNA互作建模，但方法可迁移至TF-DNA结合位点预测，与本课题相关。
abstract: The human brain develops through a tightly organized cascade of patterning events, induced by transcription factor expression and changes in chromatin accessibility. Although gene expression across the developing brain has been described at single-cell resolution(1), similar atlases of chromatin accessibility have been primarily focused on the forebrain(2-4). Here we describe chromatin accessibility and paired gene expression across the entire developing human brain during the first trimester (6-13 weeks after conception). We defined 135 clusters and used multiomic measurements to link candidate cis-regulatory elements to gene expression. The number of accessible regions increased both with age and along neuronal differentiation. Using a convolutional neural network, we identified putative functional transcription factor-binding sites in enhancers characterizing neuronal subtypes. We applied this model to cis-regulatory elements linked to ESRRB to elucidate its activation mechanism in the Purkinje cell lineage. Finally, by linking disease-associated single nucleotide polymorphisms to cis-regulatory elements, we validated putative pathogenic mechanisms in several diseases and identified midbrain-derived GABAergic neurons as being the most vulnerable to major depressive disorder-related mutations. Our findings provide a more detailed view of key gene regulatory mechanisms underlying the emergence of brain cell types during the first trimester and a comprehensive reference for future studies related to human neurodevelopment.
abstract_zh: 人脑的发育通过一系列紧密组织的模式形成事件进行，这些事件由转录因子表达和染色质可及性的变化所诱导。尽管发育中人脑的基因表达已在单细胞分辨率下被描述(1)，类似的染色质可及性图谱主要集中于前脑(2-4)。在此，我们描述了整个发育中人脑在妊娠早期（受孕后6-13周）的染色质可及性及配对的基因表达。我们定义了135个聚类，并利用多组学测量将候选顺式调控元件与基因表达联系起来。可及区域的数量随年龄和神经元分化而增加。通过使用卷积神经网络，我们识别了表征神经元亚型的增强子中潜在的功能性转录因子结合位点。我们将此模型应用于与ESRRB相关的顺式调控元件，以阐明其在浦肯野细胞谱系中的激活机制。最后，通过将疾病相关的单核苷酸多态性与顺式调控元件关联，我们验证了几种疾病中推定的致病机制，并确定中脑来源的GABA能神经元对重度抑郁障碍相关突变最为脆弱。我们的发现为妊娠早期脑细胞类型出现背后的关键基因调控机制提供了更详细的视角，并为未来与人神经发育相关的研究提供了全面的参考。
